description: Verses the classical texts themselves give as examples of a quality. pole (for mādhurya): soft | harsh | info (scored for information only) | null (not used for mādhurya). tier: primary (the root text's own example) | commentary (an example added by a commentator). script: telugu | iast (converted with common/translit.py). contrasts: pairs that a text itself sets against each other, for ojas (more / less) and prasāda (clearer / obscurer). broken_meter: verses a text gives as examples of a broken meter (ఛందోభంగము), with the pāda it says is broken in meter (broken_pada) and, where it says so, in yati (yati_broken_pada); for the chandas distance.

exemplars.note: The treatise's example of saukumārya, the quality of letters with a bindu before them (4.60).
lines: చ్చందన మొందు నిందుముఖిచందము డెందమునం దలంప నీ
జెందె నృసింహ కౌఁగిటను జేర్పుము ముందుగ మందగామినిన్.

exemplars.note: Mammaṭa's example of the letters, compounds and arrangement that manifest mādhurya. GRETIL prints 'pratiaṃ' and 'bhaṅgībhraṅgīkṛtam'; read here as 'pratimaṃ' and 'bhaṅgībhiraṅgīkṛtam', the reading of the printed editions.
The phrase the treatise gives as an example of the paruṣa (śrutikaṭu) word defect.
Mammaṭa's example of the letters, long compounds and arrangement that manifest ojas.
lines: doṣṇāṃ caiṣāṃ kimetat phalamiha nagarīrakṣaṇe yat prayāsaḥ

exemplars.note: Quoted for its 'uddhata' (vehement) arrangement and letters, chosen to suit the speaker, Bhīma.
Quoted for a vehement arrangement chosen to suit the matter described.
Daṇḍin's example of sukumāratā, a texture made mostly of non-harsh letters (aniṣṭhurākṣaraprāyam, 1.69). Its few harsh letters are scattered.
What the other school composes 'though it is hard to utter' (kṛcchrodyam api), calling it brilliant.
The commentator's example of a gāḍha (dense) texture, from Tikkana.
lines: గీర్వాణాకృతు లేవురిప్డు నిను దోర్లీలన్ వెసం గిట్టి గం
ధర్వుల్ మానముఁ బ్రాణముం గొనుట తథ్యం బెమ్మెయిం గీచకా!

exemplars.note: The commentator's example of saukumārya in Vāmana's wider sense, 'absence of harshness', from Peddana.
lines: ఎక్కడి యూరు కాల్నిలువ కింటికిఁ బోయెదనంచుఁ బల్కె దీ
వక్కట! మీ కుటీర నిలయంబులకున్ సరి రాకపోయెనే?
బిక్కడి గాంగ సైకతము లిక్కడి యీ లవలీనికుంజముల్

exemplars.note: The treatise's example of its own mādhurya, which it defines by words standing apart (no long compounds), not by sounds (4.60).
lines: వెనుకఁకు బాఱి పుల్గఱచి వేషము మార్చి బిలంబు దూఱ కా
ననమున కేఁగి సిగ్గున నణంగి భరంపడి వీఁగి తావిషం
బెనసి నతి న్భజించి నదు లీఁది భ్రమించెను రాసు లన్నియున్.

exemplars.note: The treatise's example of ojas, which it defines by compounds (4.69). The 1945 commentator remarks that it is full of compounds but not dense in texture.
Mammaṭa's example of prasāda, the quality common to every rasa and texture.

1.60 says alliteration of this kind 'brings harshness of texture and slackness' (bandhapāruṣyaṃ śaithilyaṃ ca). The verse does not say which half shows which; the first half, with its k, kh and visargas, is usually read as the harsh one.
lines: smaraḥ kharaḥ khalaḥ kāntaḥ kāyaḥ kopaś ca naḥ kṛśaḥ

exemplars.note: The other half of the same verse, usually read as the slack one.
lines: cyuto māno'dhiko rāgo moho jāto'savo gatāḥ

exemplars.note: Daṇḍin's example of a slack (śithila) texture, all unaspirated soft letters. He counts slackness a fault (1.43, 1.69), so the softest texture is not the best.
Daṇḍin's example of the ojas the easterners compose even in verse: one compound after another (1.80: ojas is abundance of compounds).
The ojas 'others want': unconfused and pleasing (anākulaṃ hṛdyam, 1.83). One compound, then plain words.
lines: kasya kāmāturaṃ ceto vāruṇī na kariṣyati

exemplars.note: Vāmana's example of ojas as a tight texture (gāḍhabandhatvam).
The same line reworded, which Vāmana gives as not tight ('na punaḥ').
The treatise's example of prasāda, which it defines by well-known words (4.57).
The example phrase of the defect aprayukta, a word poets do not use. The closing 'అనఁగన్' of the verse is left out.
The example phrase of the defect asamartha, a word used in a sense that is not established ('అప్రసిద్ధయోగంబు'). The closing 'అటన్నన్' is left out.
The example phrase of the defect apratīta, words found only in śāstras and purāṇas. The closing 'అనఁగన్' is left out.
lines: తలఁతు వృషాకపిఁ ద్రిజగము నెలమి నజావృతముఁ జేయు నీశ్వరు

exemplars.note: The example phrase of the defect kliṣṭa, a far-fetched meaning. The closing 'అనఁగన్' is left out.
Daṇḍin's example of prasāda: of well-known meaning, pleasing because understood at once (prasiddhārtham, pratītisubhagam).
What the other school accepts as 'learned' though it is not current (nātirūḍham).

contrasts.basis: The treatise: ojas is a texture full of compounds (4.69); its mādhurya is words standing apart (4.60).
Mammaṭa: long compounds for ojas (8.75), none or middling for mādhurya (8.74).
Mammaṭa: a vehement arrangement (8.77) against his mādhurya example.
Mammaṭa: a vehement arrangement (8.77) against his mādhurya example.
Vāmana's own pair for a tight texture (3.1.5).
Daṇḍin: the easterners' ojas against the unconfused ojas others want (1.82-84).
Daṇḍin: an ojas example against the verse he calls not forceful (anūrjita, 1.71).
The 1945 commentary: 4.70 is full of compounds but not dense; Tikkana's verse is dense.
The treatise: well-known words (4.57) against a word poets do not use (4.5).
The treatise: well-known words against an unestablished usage (4.8).
The treatise: well-known words against words found only in śāstras (4.15).
The treatise: well-known words against a far-fetched expression (4.17).
Daṇḍin: of well-known meaning (1.45) against the learned but not current (1.46). Sanskrit, scored with the Telugu model.

broken_meter.basis: The treatise's own example of ఛందోభంగము. The commentary: 'ఇట రెండవపాదమున ఛందోభంగము. కందమున ద్వితీయ పాదాంత వర్ణము గురువై యుండవలెను. ఇట లఘువుగానే యున్నది.' (the last akshara of a kandamu's second pāda must be guru; here it is laghu). The commentary adds: 'నాల్గవ పాదమున యతిభంగము' (the yati is broken in the fourth pāda).
broken_meter.note: Lines 1-3 as the 1945 commentary reads them. Line 4 is from the 1920 edition, because the OCR of the 1945 text is damaged there. The 1920 edition prints line 2 with నితఁడున్, which mends the meter.

broken_meter.basis: The commentator's example from Chalamacharla Raṅgācārya's Āndhra Pratāparudra Yaśobhūṣaṇamu: 'ఇట మూఁడవపాదమున ఛందోభంగమయినది' (here the meter is broken in the third pāda).
broken_meter.note: As printed in the 1945 commentary (OCR text).
